opportunities.title: Creme Bars 'Pinky Up' TV/CTV spot -> scannable spot with sweepstakes and media attribution
opportunities.what_is_happening: Hershey's launched Salted Caramel and Affogato Creme Bars in September 2026 with a KATSEYE 'Pinky Up' commercial. The campaign spans CTV, national TV, digital video, display, paid social, streaming audio, influencer and earned media, and the TV signal shows no QR code or link.
opportunities.why_flowcode: A national TV and CTV buy with no scannable next step cannot show which network or creative drove trial. A Flowcode in the spot leading to a FlowHub (KATSEYE content, sweepstakes, where-to-buy), with Analytics by network, turns viewers into measurable connections and first-party contacts.
opportunities.confidence_why: Two agreeing trade-press signals, and PIM Brands is a close match (snack brand, celebrity-led sweepstakes in a multi-network TV spot).
opportunities.size_why: National TV plus CTV for a new Hershey's line.
opportunities.timing_why: The launch spot aired in September; the realistic entry point is the next flight or a creative refresh.
opportunities.suggested_play: Add a Flowcode to the next 'Pinky Up' flight and the CTV cut, leading to a Creme Bars FlowHub with a KATSEYE-themed sweepstakes and a store locator. Use per-network codes so Analytics show which placements drive scans and entries, as PIM Brands did to shift media mid-campaign (32k new contacts captured, 56% conversion rate, 93% net new).
opportunities.first_step: Ask the Hershey's Creme Bars brand team which TV and CTV flights are still to be bought or refreshed, and send them the PIM Brands case study.

opportunities.title: Grinch holiday packs and Kisses foil kit -> on-pack sweepstakes with CRM capture
opportunities.what_is_happening: Hershey's 2026 holiday lineup includes limited-edition Grinch-themed packaging and a limited-edition Hershey's Kisses gift-wrapping foil kit. The kit is sold online at shop.hersheys.com/holiday on Cyber Monday, Nov. 30; the signal notes links or QR codes are already in use.
opportunities.why_flowcode: Licensed, limited-edition packs reach shoppers nationally but turn few of them into first-party data. A Flowcode on the pack that leads to a FlowHub sweepstakes, with entries captured in FlowID, turns each scan into a CRM contact. The destination can be changed after printing for later campaigns.
opportunities.confidence_why: The brand's own press release, and Capri Sun is a close match (front-of-pack sweepstakes on a national snack brand). Existing link use makes the sale easier but may mean a competitor to replace.
opportunities.size_why: Seasonal packaging on a national confectionery brand.
opportunities.timing_why: The 2026 holiday packs are already produced; the realistic pitch is the 2027 holiday and seasonal runs.
opportunities.suggested_play: For the next holiday or licensed run, put a front-of-pack Flowcode that leads to a FlowHub sweepstakes, with a holiday recipe or gift-wrap idea and a link to shop.hersheys.com. Capture every entrant in FlowID with sync to Hershey's CRM, the approach behind Capri Sun's 28K+ sweepstakes submissions.
opportunities.first_step: Ask the Hershey's seasonal brand manager how the current holiday packs use QR codes or links and when 2027 holiday packaging art is locked.

opportunities.what_is_happening: The Creme Bars 'Pinky Up' campaign runs on paid social and with influencers alongside CTV and national TV. The signal shows no tracked links in use.
opportunities.why_flowcode: Creator and social posts with no branded link cannot be tied to the people who also saw or scanned the TV spot. FlowURLs in creator posts that lead to the same FlowHub and FlowID give Hershey's one view of digital and offline connections.
opportunities.confidence_why: One trade-press source; Waterpik is a decent match (branded short URL in digital channels leading to a sweepstakes and opt-in), though it is not food.
opportunities.size_why: A multi-channel national social and influencer program.

opportunities.title: Reese's Pie bakery expansion -> Flowcodes on the box and warehouse-club displays
opportunities.what_is_happening: Reese's is bringing back the supersized Reese's Pie as a Thanksgiving dessert. It is sold at shop.hersheys.com from Nov. 16, 2026 for $49.99 (limit 2 per order) and in limited quantities at select warehouse club locations. Trade press frames it as moving Reese's into dessert and bakery, beyond the candy aisle.
opportunities.why_flowcode: A returning, limited product sold in select club stores has no measurable link between in-store displays and the online shop. Flowcodes on the box and club displays, measured by location in Analytics and leading to a FlowHub (online order, serving ideas, store availability), show which locations convert.
opportunities.confidence_why: The brand's own release plus trade-press agreement, but Eddie Bauer (apparel tags) is only a decent retail match.
opportunities.size_why: Select warehouse club locations and online sales of a limited-quantity item.
opportunities.timing_why: This year's run is on sale; the product is returning, so the pitch is next year's run.
opportunities.suggested_play: For the next Reese's Pie run, give each warehouse-club display its own Flowcode leading to a FlowHub with online ordering, serving ideas and availability. Use Analytics by location to see which stores convert, as Eddie Bauer did with dynamic in-store codes (183% YoY scan growth, 167K all-time connections).
opportunities.first_step: Contact the Reese's shopper marketing lead to ask how warehouse-club sell-through is measured for Reese's Pie and propose location-coded displays for the next run.

opportunities.title: Reese's and Creme Bars pop-ups and sampling -> first-party capture at activations
opportunities.what_is_happening: Reese's and The Nitro Bar gave away up to 1,000 Reese's Pumpkins PB Whip Lattes a day at a free NYC pop-up on Sept. 14-15, 2026, each with a recipe card and Reese's Pumpkins. Sampling, pop-ups and an Uber partnership were planned to follow the Creme Bars launch, and neither signal shows a QR code or link.
opportunities.why_flowcode: Free giveaways and recipe cards reach thousands of people but capture no first-party data. A Flowcode on recipe cards and signage, leading to a FlowHub, with Smart Rules to block duplicate claims and FlowID to keep each visitor as a Hershey contact, closes that gap.
opportunities.confidence_why: The pop-up comes from a secondary source, and Feld's citywide claim mechanic is only a loose analogy for a product sampling event.
opportunities.size_why: A single-city pop-up, with Creme Bars activations of unknown scale.
opportunities.timing_why: The NYC pop-up has ended; the pitch is the next seasonal activation or any Creme Bars sampling not yet produced.
opportunities.suggested_play: At the next Reese's or Hershey's pop-up, print a Flowcode on every recipe card and sampling sign that leads to a FlowHub with the recipe, a sweepstakes and an email opt-in. Smart Rules cap claims per person, as Feld did in its 20-code Tampa hunt, and FlowID keeps each visitor as a first-party contact.
opportunities.first_step: Ask the Hershey's experiential team for the calendar of upcoming Creme Bars sampling and seasonal pop-ups, and offer to code the recipe cards for the next one.

play.name: Event and sponsorship capture
